body.heading: Familiarity dims the light
paragraphs: Early in a relationship, everything about the other person is interesting data. Years in, the brain files them under 'known' and stops paying attention — not from lack of love, but from efficiency.
The cost is real. People bloom under attention and wilt without it, and a partner who feels unseen will slowly go looking for the feeling elsewhere — in work, in hobbies, in distance.

body.heading: Attention as a practice
paragraphs: Once a day, deliberately notice one thing: how they handled something, what they are reading, the mood they came home in. Mention it. Being noticed is the whole gift.

Ask questions you do not know the answer to. Even after twenty years, there are some — what they dream about now, what they would do with a free month. Curiosity is not just a phase of love; it is a practice of it.

description: Long love goes quiet in one specific way: we stop noticing. Deliberate attention brings a familiar person back into focus.
